attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as router between lan-a (eth1, trusted, paired with node2) and lan-b (eth2, guest, paired with node3): static IPs 10.10.1.1/24 and 10.10.2.1/24, firewall zone 'lana' (input/output/forward=ACCEPT) and zone 'lanb' (input=REJECT, output=ACCEPT, forward=REJECT), a lana->lanb forwarding rule for full trusted-to-guest access, and explicit lanb input-allow rules limited to DNS (53/udp+tcp) and DHCP (67/udp) so guests can reach node1's own services. Enabled dnsmasq DHCP+DNS on both interfaces. On node2/node3 added systemd-networkd overrides for enp8s0 (DHCP for addressing, UseRoutes=no, plus a static route to the other subnet via node1) so return/forward traffic routes correctly through node1. Verified end-to-end: guest can resolve DNS via node1 but cannot ping or open a TCP connection to the trusted host (connection refused/port unreachable), while the trusted host can ping and open a TCP connection to the guest host. All three nodes were restarted one at a time via native `reboot`; each showed a changed kernel boot_id after recovery, and post-restart checks reconfirmed persisted config (UCI firewall/network, dnsmasq running, DHCP leases/routes) and the same isolation/access behavior. The shared 10.100.69.0/24 network (used for Harbor exec access to all three nodes) was left untouched per the management-path preservation rule, since it is out-of-band from the lan-a/lan-b topology being tested.
